newsitem.title: JAPAN: Early Asia oil falls, Mideast grades take backseat.
newsitem.headline: Early Asia oil falls, Mideast grades take backseat.

text.p: Global bearishness in Western markets weighed on oil prices in early Asia as well, with broker's assessments for August cash Brent falling to $17.75/17.85, a 15 cent drop from Wednesday levels.
Futures exchanges in London and New York fell by 44 cents and 31 cents, respectively Wednesday, as markets digested U.S. data indicating heavy supply, excessive imports, and only moderate demand.

Asian traders remained focused on West African dealings, with Middle East grades still quiet. South Korean refiners, fresh off reported deals for Congo grades Djeno and N'Kossa, now appear to have their sights on a two million barrel parcel of Nigerian Bonny Light, traders said.
"There's going to be a lot of Middle East barrels lying around when this West African frenzy is through," said one Japanese trader.
Brent/Dubai play continued on the trend, with an August deal heard done at 90 cents and a September reported at $1.05, both in line with day-earlier levels.
Dubai markets, stuck in a front-month contango, drew speculative attention, with an October/February Dubai reported done at plus 12 cents, from a Wall Street trader to a U.S. trader, traders said.
